notes: Discipline priest healer rotation, written against the fork's fake raid: the healer is raid player 0, the four fake party members are players 1 to 4 and the tank is player 5. Reference build: 33 points in Discipline and 18 in Holy (engine talent string 005203031305101531-0350500302: Twin Disciplines 5, Silent Resolve 2, Improved Power Word: Shield 3, Mental Agility 3, Inner Focus, Meditation 3, Mental Strength 5, Soul Warding, Penance, Renewed Hope 5, Divine Aegis 3, Power Infusion; Improved Renew 3, Holy Specialization 5, Divine Fury 5, Inspiration 3, Improved Healing 2). Penance is cast on its cooldown at whoever is hurt, the tank is shielded when he is hurt and Weakened Soul is off, and the filler is Heal. Power Infusion is only used when the player names a target for it; the major-cooldown pass casts it. Renew is left out on purpose: against the fork's test profile it returned less health per mana than Penance and Heal. Mana: the list opens with the autocast line, which is how the Major Mana Potion, the Demonic Rune and Inner Focus are used (each fires whenever it is ready and the bar has room for it; Inner Focus goes on whichever priest spell is cast next). Dark Sacrifice follows the autocast line behind a mana gate (below 70% mana with the healer's own health above 70%). Mana pacing: the filler, Prayer of Healing and Power Word: Shield fire at their normal thresholds only while the mana bar is at least 90% of the share of the fight left (currentManaPercent against remainingTimePercent); behind that pace the filler waits for a tank under 50% and a member under 35% and the shield waits. Penance and the emergency Flash Heals are never paced. Ranks follow one rule, stated in design/reviews/2026-10-08-healer-mana-audit.md: starting from the top ranks, a lower rank (never one learned below level 20) is taken for a spell when it raises the ranker's guarded score by more than two percent, the biggest gain first, the tank's casts and the party members' casts counted apart, and compared on the raid gear the ranker published for the list being tried. The engine states the client's own numbers for every rank with no downrank penalty, so a lower rank is a statement about this profile, not a measurement of the game. The site runs this list as written at band 60 and lifts every ranked spell to the highest rank learned below it. Here that is Power Word: Shield at rank 4; every other spell keeps the top rank a trainer teaches (Prayer of Healing rank 5, Greater Heal rank 5 and Renew rank 10 are Ahn'Qiraj book ranks, so their tops in Phase 1 are ranks 4, 4 and 9). The comparison is repeated on the gear each new list makes the ranker choose until no spell moves. The review lists what each rank returned. Round-3 audit (design/reviews/2026-11-01-sim-audit-round3/casters.md): Shadowfiend (401977) is not cast; a Forever priest cannot learn it (no learn level on its skill-line row, and no beta priest ever cast it). Lightwell is placed before the pull (a prepull cast, 365 mana at rank 3): the fake raid members the damage model hurts click it for a renew each, five charges, and its client rows are 320 health every 2 seconds for 10 seconds that being attacked cancels, so over the profile it returned about 1.4 percent more effective healing and 8 more seconds of mana than the same list without it (spec-breakdown -heal, 2026-10-08, design/reviews/2026-10-08-remaining-trainables.md). Client 1.60.1.70707 review (2026-10-31): Renew on the tank (rank 3, the Holy list's line) now follows Power Word: Shield; the page and the build's Improved Renew 3/3 had promised it while the list never cast it. About +2% healing and +10% guarded score in heal-builds, and it makes Improved Renew worth about +1% over the same points elsewhere. Round 6 (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round6/healers.md): the heal profile's raid-wide pulses now land on the healer as well, three of the five members of the group a pulse. Round 6 also changed two lines: the tank's filler is Greater Heal instead of Heal (the party members keep Heal), and the party members' emergency Flash Heals are paced (mana at least 70% of the share of the fight left). Together about +4% effective healing; the list had never cast Greater Heal. Binding Heal (taught from the Holy skill line since the 70707 hotfix push) now stands in front of every emergency Flash Heal while you are under 90 percent health: the raid pulses reach you, and it heals you as much as its target for Flash Heal's mana (about +8% effective healing in the round-6 run). The Holy list keeps Flash Heal: Holy Binding already heals you off it, and Binding Heal added under 1% there.

priorityList.notes: Dark Sacrifice when the mana bar has room and you are not hurt. It trades your own health for mana over fifteen seconds and adds your Spirit to the mana, and its ten minute cooldown makes it a once-a-fight cast.
Penance on its 12 second cooldown: three pulses for the price of one cast and the best healing per mana the Discipline kit has.

On a hurt tank whenever Weakened Soul is off him. Soul Warding makes it free of cooldown and 15% cheaper. Rank 4 is the rank this profile pays for: it costs about a third of the top rank's mana and returned more guarded score. Renewed Hope also turns the Weakened Soul into extra crit chance and Divine Aegis for the heals that follow.
Renew stays on the tank for the whole fight at a cheap rank: a cheaper rank returns more health per mana for the spell power it is cast with, and the dearer ranks cost the mana the fight runs out of.
Binding Heal in place of the Flash Heal below it while you are under 90 percent yourself: same cost and cast, and it heals you as much as the target.
Flash Heal is the fast heal and the dear one: it is only for a tank that is genuinely low.
